diagnostics.message: `helm_release.karpenter` has `depends_on = [null_resource.wait_for_cluster]`, but that ordering is already established transitively: helm_release.karpenter references `module.karpenter` (implicit dep), `module.karpenter` declares `depends_on = [null_resource.patch_calico_installation]`, `patch_calico` references `data.external.update_kubeconfig` (implicit), and that data source declares `depends_on = [null_resource.wait_for_cluster]`. So wait_for_cluster is already an ancestor of the release. (The helm provider is also configured from `data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster`/`data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.cluster`, which both depend on `null_resource.wait_for_cluster`.) The explicit `depends_on` is therefore redundant.

The Karpenter controller runs as an EKS Pod Identity consumer: `module.karpenter` sets `create_pod_identity_association = true`, so the controller's service account gets its AWS credentials via EKS Pod Identity. EKS Pod Identity only works once the `eks-pod-identity-agent` add-on (`aws_eks_addon.eks_pod_identity_agent`) is actually running on the nodes. `helm_release.karpenter` has no dependency (direct or transitive) on that add-on — it only depends on the cluster/`module.karpenter`, both of which are ordered *before* the node group and the agent addon. As a result the Karpenter controller can be deployed before the pod identity agent is ready and fail to obtain credentials. (In the canonical terraform-aws-modules example the agent lives inside `module.eks`, which gives this ordering implicitly; here it was split into a standalone resource and the ordering was lost.) Adding `depends_on = [aws_eks_addon.eks_pod_identity_agent]` (or ordering `module.karpenter` after it) closes the gap; there is no clean attribute reference on the add-on to wire it idiomatically.
